question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.
Solomon always refers in the dictionary for clearing doubts about words.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. to the dictionary.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "refer", when used in the sense of consulting a source (like a dictionary, book, or manual) for information, is followed by the preposition "to" — the correct phrasal form is "refer to".
◦ Example: Whenever I face a difficult word, I refer to the dictionary.

• In the given sentence, "Solomon always refers in the dictionary" wrongly uses the preposition "in" instead of "to". The correct sentence is: "Solomon always refers to the dictionary for clearing doubts about words."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "on the dictionary" is incorrect because "refer" never takes the preposition "on" in this sense.

• Option 2: "No substitution" is incorrect because the original sentence does contain a preposition error that needs correction.

• Option 4: "with the dictionary" is incorrect because "refer with" is not a standard collocation in English.

NOTE

• Other commonly confused prepositional verbs tested by SSC: "apply for" (a job), "depend on", "consist of", "agree with" (a person)/"agree to" (a proposal), and "differ from" (a thing)/"differ with" (an opinion).

• Remember: "refer to" = to consult or mention; "refer as" = to call/describe someone as something (e.g. "He is referred to as a genius.")

question:
In the given sentence the underlined word may have been incorrectly spelt. Identify the option that rectifies the spelling. If there is no error in spelling, select 'No error'.
Siraz-ud-Daula beseiged Calcutta to take punitive actions against the East India Company.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. besieged.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "besieged" — the past tense of "besiege", meaning to surround a place with armed forces in order to capture it, or to crowd around someone/something. (घेराबंदी करना)
◦ Example: The army besieged the fort for several months before it finally surrendered.

• Spelling key: B + E + SIEGE + D. Remember the base word "siege" (a blockade), and simply add "be-" at the front and "-d" at the end for the past tense. Note the "ie" sequence (i before e), not "ei".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "besiezed" is incorrect because the letter "g" has been wrongly replaced with "z".

• Option 2: "besiejed" is incorrect because the letter "g" has been wrongly replaced with "j".

• Option 4: "No error" is incorrect because the given spelling "beseiged" wrongly places "e" before "i" in the root word.

NOTE

• The rule "i before e except after c" is generally reliable for such words: believe, siege, niece, relieve, but receive, ceiling, deceive (after "c").

• Related words with the same root: siege (noun), besieger (one who besieges), besieging (present participle).

question:
In the given sentence the underlined word may have been incorrectly spelt. Identify the option that rectifies the spelling. If there is no error in spelling, select 'No error'.
The adoloscent period of life, one of the most difficult stages of development, is known as the period of stress and storm.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. adolescent.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling is "adolescent" — relating to the period of life between childhood and adulthood; a young person undergoing this transition. (किशोरावस्था से संबंधित)
◦ Example: Adolescent students often experience rapid emotional and physical changes.

• Spelling key: A + DO + LES + CENT. The word comes from the Latin "adolescere" (to grow up). Note the sequence "o-l-e-s", and the ending "-escent" (as in "crescent", "convalescent").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "adelescent" is incorrect because the "o" after "ad" has been wrongly replaced with "e".

• Option 3: "adeloscent" is incorrect because it wrongly replaces "o" with "e" and also reverses the letters "e" and "o" in the middle syllable.

• Option 4: "No error" is incorrect because the given word "adoloscent" wrongly spells the middle syllable as "olo" instead of "ole".

NOTE

• The related noun is adolescence (the period itself), following the same root spelling pattern.

• Other words ending in "-escent": convalescent, obsolescent, luminescent, effervescent — all keep the "e" before "scent".

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.
Mandeep has repaired the truck.
option_1: The truck have been repaired by Mandeep.
option_2: The truck had been repaired by Mandeep.
option_3: The truck is been repaired by Mandeep.
option_4: The truck has been repaired by Mandeep.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. The truck has been repaired by Mandeep.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "Mandeep has repaired the truck" is an assertive sentence in the Present Perfect Tense.

• Rule — Present Perfect Tense:
◦ Active: Subject + has/have + V3 + Object
◦ Passive: Object + has/have been + V3 + by + Subject

• Applying the rule: the object "the truck" becomes the subject; it is singular (third person), so the auxiliary is "has"; the verb "repaired" is already the past participle (V3); and "Mandeep" becomes the agent with "by".
◦ Passive: The truck has been repaired by Mandeep.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because "have been repaired" wrongly uses the plural auxiliary "have" with the singular subject "the truck"; it should be "has".

• Option 2 is incorrect because "had been repaired" is the passive form of the Past Perfect Tense, not the Present Perfect Tense.

• Option 3 is incorrect because "is been repaired" is an ungrammatical combination — "is" and "been" cannot be used together in this way; the correct auxiliary for present perfect passive is "has/have been".

NOTE

• The auxiliary in present perfect passive always agrees in number with the new subject (the former object): has been for singular, have been for plural.

• Common error to avoid: mixing tenses, e.g. using "is/are been", which is grammatically invalid in Standard English.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.
The man supervising the exam had a huge moustache.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Invigilator.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Invigilator" means a person who supervises students during an examination to ensure that no unfair means are used. (परीक्षा निरीक्षक)
◦ Example: The invigilator walked up and down the rows to prevent cheating during the exam.

• The given phrase "the man supervising the exam" exactly describes the role of an invigilator, hence it is the most appropriate one-word substitute.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: Examiner (परीक्षक): A person who sets or evaluates/assesses an examination or test, not one who merely supervises it while it is being conducted.

• Option 2: Curator (संग्रहाध्यक्ष): A person who is in charge of a museum, art gallery, or exhibition.

• Option 3: Controller (नियंत्रक): A person who manages or regulates an organisation's affairs or finances; too general and not specific to exam supervision.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes often asked by SSC: Invigilator (supervises an exam), Examiner (sets/checks an exam), Examinee (one who takes an exam), Proctor (American English equivalent of invigilator).

question:
Rearrange the parts of the sentence in correct order.
A single uranium
P. pencil eraser, contains the same energy
Q. pellet, slightly larger than a
R. as a ton of coal, 3 barrels of oil
S. or 17,000 cubic feet of natural gas
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. QPRS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• To arrange jumbled parts correctly, first identify the part that logically and grammatically continues from the fixed opening phrase, then trace the chain of ideas to its natural conclusion.

• The fixed part "A single uranium" must be followed by Q ("pellet, slightly larger than a") to complete the noun phrase "A single uranium pellet, slightly larger than a...".

• This is naturally followed by P ("pencil eraser, contains the same energy"), completing the comparison "...slightly larger than a pencil eraser, contains the same energy..." and introducing the object of comparison for the energy.

• R ("as a ton of coal, 3 barrels of oil") logically follows to list the first two energy equivalents: "...the same energy as a ton of coal, 3 barrels of oil...".

• Finally, S ("or 17,000 cubic feet of natural gas") completes the list with the final alternative, joined by "or".

• Full sentence: "A single uranium pellet, slightly larger than a pencil eraser, contains the same energy as a ton of coal, 3 barrels of oil, or 17,000 cubic feet of natural gas."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. QPRS.

Additional Information

• Option 1: PRSQ is incorrect because it places P (which needs the noun "pellet" from Q to make sense) immediately after the opening, producing the meaningless phrase "A single uranium pencil eraser...".

• Option 2: RSPQ is incorrect because it starts the comparison ("as a ton of coal...") before the object being compared ("contains the same energy") has even been introduced.

• Option 4: RPQS is incorrect for the same reason as Option 2 — it opens with R, which cannot logically follow "A single uranium" without Q and P first establishing the pellet and its comparison.

NOTE

• In para/sentence-jumble questions, always look for a part containing a linking word (and, but, or, as, so) or a pronoun (it, this, that) — such parts usually cannot open the sequence and must follow the part they refer back to.

• Here, R begins with "as", which signals it must follow a comparative expression ("the same energy as..."), ruling out any order that places R too early.

question:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.
Mr. Sharma asked him if Maya had invited him for lunch.
option_1: Mr. Sharma said to him, "Has Maya invited you for lunch?"
option_2: Mr. Sharma said to me, "Has Maya invited you for lunch?"
option_3: Mr. Sharma said to him, "Had Maya invited us for lunch?"
option_4: Mr. Sharma said to him, "Did Maya invited us for lunch?"
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Mr. Sharma said to him, "Has Maya invited you for lunch?"

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The given sentence is in indirect (reported) speech, reporting a question (an interrogative sentence) introduced by "if/whether".

• Rule — converting reported questions (yes/no type) to direct speech:
◦ The reporting verb "asked" changes back to "said to", and the connector "if/whether" is dropped.
◦ The word order is inverted back to a question, and a question mark is added inside the quotation marks.
◦ The reported verb "had invited" (past perfect, used to report a simple past/present perfect action) is converted back to "has invited", since the original question would have been asked in the present perfect ("Has Maya invited...").
◦ Pronouns are reversed to match the original speaker's perspective: "him" (object, referring to the listener) becomes "you" in direct speech, since Mr. Sharma is speaking directly to that person.

• Applying the rule: Mr. Sharma said to him, "Has Maya invited you for lunch?"

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is incorrect because it uses "said to me" instead of "said to him" — there is no first-person speaker ("me") involved in the original sentence; the reported subject is a third person ("him").

• Option 3 is incorrect because "Had Maya invited us for lunch?" wrongly keeps the past perfect "had" instead of converting it back to "has", and wrongly uses "us" instead of "you".

• Option 4 is incorrect because "Did Maya invited us for lunch?" is grammatically wrong — the auxiliary "Did" must be followed by the base form "invite", not the past form "invited"; it also wrongly uses "us" instead of "you".

NOTE

• In direct-to-indirect (and vice versa) conversions of questions, always check three things together: the reporting verb (say/said to ↔ ask/asked), the tense of the reported verb, and the pronouns, as SSC often manipulates just one of these to create a wrong option.

• For yes/no questions, indirect speech uses if/whether; for wh-questions, the wh-word itself is retained (e.g. "He asked where I lived").

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the following sentence.
Listening to the news of his father's illness, Soumen left for home with a heavy heart.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. sickness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Illness" means the state of being unwell or in poor health; a disease or sickness. (बीमारी)
◦ Example: Her prolonged illness kept her away from school for a month.

• "Sickness" is the closest synonym, as it also refers to the state of being unwell or suffering from a disease.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "disturbance" (अशांति/बाधा): A disruption of peace or a normal state of affairs; not related to physical health.

• Option 3: "disintegration" (विघटन): The process of breaking up into small parts or pieces; used for objects, structures, or systems, not for a person's health.

• Option 4: "disorder" (अव्यवस्था/विकार): Can sometimes relate to a medical condition (e.g. "a mental disorder"), but in general usage it more commonly means a lack of order or organisation, and is not as precise a synonym of "illness" as "sickness".

NOTE

• Other common synonyms of illness: ailment, malady, infirmity, indisposition.

• Do not confuse "disorder" (a specific medical/psychological condition, or a lack of order) with "illness" (the general state of being unwell) in synonym-based questions — SSC often uses this as a close distractor.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.
The jewel thief was punished by the judge.
option_1: Punishment had been given to jewel thief.
option_2: The police had punished the jewel thief.
option_3: The judge punished the jewel thief.
option_4: Punishment was given to jewel thief.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. The judge punished the jewel thief.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence "The jewel thief was punished by the judge" is a passive sentence in the Simple Past Tense.

• Rule — Simple Past Tense:
◦ Passive: Object + was/were + V3 + by + Subject
◦ Active: Subject + V2 + Object

• Applying the rule: the agent "the judge" (introduced by "by") becomes the subject; the verb "punished" (V3) becomes the simple past "punished" (V2, same form here); and "the jewel thief" becomes the object.
◦ Active: The judge punished the jewel thief.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 is incorrect because it remains in a passive-like construction ("Punishment had been given to") and also introduces the past perfect tense, which is not equivalent to the original simple past sentence.

• Option 2 is incorrect because it introduces "the police" as the subject, which is not the agent mentioned in the original sentence ("by the judge"); the subject of an active sentence must match the doer named in the passive sentence.

• Option 4 is incorrect for the same reason as Option 1 — it keeps a passive-style structure ("Punishment was given to") instead of converting fully to the active voice, and also drops the agent ("the judge") entirely.

NOTE

• When converting passive to active, the agent introduced by "by" in the passive sentence must always become the subject of the active sentence — never replace it with an unrelated noun.

• If a passive sentence has no "by + agent" phrase, a suitable subject (like "someone", "people", "they") is used while converting to active voice.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
The little boy demanded colourful balloons, ribbons in the village fair. When the father didn't pay heed to his demands, the boy made a________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. wry face.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to make a wry face" means to twist one's face to show displeasure, disgust, or disappointment. (नाराज़गी या अनिच्छा में मुँह बनाना)
◦ Example: When told to eat the bitter medicine, the child made a wry face.

• In the given sentence, since the father did not pay heed to the boy's demands, the boy naturally expressed his displeasure by making a wry face.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "cloven hoof" (शैतानी प्रवृत्ति दिखाना): To show one's true, often evil or mischievous, nature or intentions — unrelated to expressing displeasure on one's face.

• Option 3: "a far cry" (बिल्कुल अलग होना): Something that is very different from something else; used to indicate a big contrast, not a facial expression.

• Option 4: "jaundiced eye" (पूर्वाग्रह से देखना): To view something with prejudice, envy, or a biased/negative attitude — not about a facial expression of momentary displeasure.

NOTE

• Related idioms with "face": "to keep a straight face" (to not laugh/smile), "to lose face" (to be humiliated), "to face the music" (to accept criticism/punishment).

• Do not confuse "wry face" (a twisted expression of displeasure) with "wry smile" (a smile showing mild, ironic amusement) — both use "wry" but convey different shades of meaning.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.
The present paper throws light on the nexus between the academic performance and mental health of children.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Link.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Nexus" means a connection or series of connections linking two or more things. (संबंध/कड़ी)
◦ Example: Researchers have found a nexus between poor sleep and reduced concentration.

• "Link" is the closest synonym, as it also refers to a connection between two things.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Dispute" (विवाद): A disagreement or argument; the opposite sense of a connection.

• Option 2: "Alignment" (संरेखण): The proper positioning or arrangement of things in relation to each other, or agreement with a policy/group — not the same as a causal or relational connection.

• Option 4: "Incongruence" (असंगति): A lack of agreement or compatibility between things — essentially opposite in meaning to "nexus".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "nexus": bond, tie, linkage, connection, relationship.

• "Nexus" is often used in academic/formal writing to describe a causal or correlational relationship between two abstract concepts, as in the given sentence.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and complete the collocation.
Every time my boss comes up with some good idea, he gets into ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. trouble.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "To get into trouble" is a standard collocation meaning to find oneself in a difficult, problematic, or embarrassing situation. (मुसीबत में पड़ना)
◦ Example: He always gets into trouble for arriving late to meetings.

• The sentence implies a mildly ironic situation — every time the boss has a good idea, it somehow lands him (or others) in difficulty — which is best expressed by "gets into trouble".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "fun" — "gets into fun" is not a standard English collocation; "fun" collocates with verbs like "have fun" or "make fun of", not "get into".

• Option 3: "sleep" — "gets into sleep" is not idiomatic; the correct collocation is "falls asleep" or "goes to sleep".

• Option 4: "shock" — "gets into shock" is not a standard collocation; the correct form would be "goes into shock" (medical context) or "is shocked".

NOTE

• Common collocations with "get into": get into trouble, get into a habit, get into a fight, get into the habit of, get into shape.

• Distinguish from "go into", used with states like shock, hiding, labour (e.g. "go into shock", "go into hiding").

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
One of my friends is gone to Goa for a holiday.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. has gone.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is "One of my friends" — in such constructions ("One of + plural noun"), the verb always agrees with "One", which is singular, and takes a third-person singular verb form.

• "Gone" is the past participle of "go", and needs a suitable auxiliary to form a correct tense; "is gone" is an incorrect construction in Standard English for describing a completed action of travelling.

• The correct form to express that the person has left for Goa is the Present Perfect Tense: Subject + has/have + V3. Since the subject is singular ("One"), the auxiliary must be "has".
◦ Correct sentence: "One of my friends has gone to Goa for a holiday."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "are gone" is incorrect because "are" is a plural auxiliary, which does not agree with the singular subject "One".

• Option 3: "gone" alone is incorrect because a past participle cannot function as the main verb of a sentence without an auxiliary verb.

• Option 4: "were gone" is incorrect because it is both a plural and a past-tense auxiliary, which agrees with neither the singular subject nor the intended present-perfect meaning.

NOTE

• With "one of the + plural noun" as subject, always use a singular verb: e.g. "One of the students has submitted the assignment."

• "Has/have gone" (present perfect of "go") should not be confused with "has/have been" (present perfect of "be", used when someone has visited and returned).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.
Neither the doctors nor / the nurse were present / when the patient / reached the hospital.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. the nurse were present.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rule — Subject-Verb agreement with "Neither...nor" / "Either...or": when two subjects of different number (one singular, one plural) are joined by "neither...nor" or "either...or", the verb agrees with the subject that is nearer to it (the principle of proximity).

• In the given sentence, the subjects are "the doctors" (plural) and "the nurse" (singular), joined by "neither...nor". Since "the nurse" (singular) is nearer to the verb, the verb must also be singular: "was", not "were".

• Corrected sentence: "Neither the doctors nor the nurse was present when the patient reached the hospital."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Neither the doctors nor" is grammatically correct as it stands; it merely sets up the correlative conjunction.

• Option 3: "when the patient" is correct; it introduces the subordinate clause correctly with no grammatical error.

• Option 4: "reached the hospital." is correct — "reached" is the appropriate simple past tense verb for the subordinate clause about the patient's arrival.

NOTE

• The proximity rule also applies to "either...or": e.g. "Either the teacher or the students are responsible."

• If both subjects are plural, the verb is plural regardless of order: "Neither the boys nor the girls were present." If both are singular, the verb is singular: "Neither the boy nor the girl was present."

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.
Although I have a good job, I wish to take the _______ of starting my own business.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. risk.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "To take the risk of (doing something)" is a standard collocation meaning to accept the possibility of danger, failure, or loss in order to achieve something. (जोखिम उठाना)
◦ Example: She decided to take the risk of investing her savings in a new venture.

• The sentence contrasts having a secure, good job with the uncertain venture of starting one's own business — this contrast is best captured by "risk", which conveys the uncertainty involved in leaving a stable job.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "back" — "take the back of" is not a meaningful or standard collocation in this context.

• Option 2: "seat" — "take a seat" is a common phrase, but "take the seat of starting my own business" is meaningless.

• Option 3: "look" — "take a look" is a common phrase meaning to glance/examine, but "take the look of starting" does not fit the sentence's meaning.

NOTE

• Related expressions: "to run the risk of" (to be in danger of), "at risk" (in a dangerous situation), "to risk it" (to take a chance).

• Common SSC collocations with "take": take a chance, take a stand, take a decision, take initiative, take responsibility.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word to fill in the blank.
If we want to progress, we must sometimes embrace __________ (mutate).
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. change.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mutate" means to change or cause to change in form or nature. (बदलना/रूपांतरित होना)
◦ Example: The virus is known to mutate rapidly, making it difficult to develop a lasting vaccine.

• "Change" is the closest and most general synonym that fits the sentence: "If we want to progress, we must sometimes embrace change."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "replicate" (प्रतिकृति बनाना): To make an exact copy of something; this is nearly the opposite of "mutate", which implies a change rather than an identical copy.

• Option 2: "imitate" (नकल करना): To copy the behaviour or appearance of someone/something else; again more about copying than changing.

• Option 4: "incise" (चीरा लगाना): To cut into something with a sharp tool; entirely unrelated in meaning to "mutate".

NOTE

• Related biology-linked vocabulary often tested by SSC: mutation (a change in genetic structure), adapt (to adjust to new conditions), evolve (to develop gradually), transform (to change markedly in form).

• Do not confuse "mutate" (to change/alter) with "replicate" (to copy/duplicate) — they are frequently placed as close distractors.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No substitution'.
Finally, here are a few examples of passages and their précis.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. No substitution.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "examples of passages and their précis" is grammatically correct as it stands: "examples of" is the correct preposition pairing ("an example of something"), and "their précis" correctly uses the possessive pronoun "their" (referring back to "passages") along with the correctly spelled word "précis" (a summary).

• Since there is no grammatical, spelling, or usage error in the underlined segment, no substitution is required.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "by passages and their précis" is incorrect because "examples by" is not correct usage — it should be "examples of".

• Option 2: "of passages and there precis" is incorrect because it wrongly replaces the possessive pronoun "their" with the adverb "there", and also drops the accent from "précis".

• Option 3: "of passages and there precises" is incorrect for the same "there/their" confusion, and additionally wrongly pluralises "précis" as "precises" — the word "précis" is invariable and has the same form in singular and plural.

NOTE

• "Their" (possessive pronoun) must never be confused with "there" (adverb of place) or "they're" (contraction of "they are") — a very common SSC error-spotting trap.

• "Précis" is a French loanword meaning a concise summary; it is spelt with an acute accent on the "e" and does not change form in the plural, unlike most English nouns.

question:
The question below consists of a set of labeled sentences. Out of the four options given, select the most logical order of the sentences to form a coherent paragraph.
P. As a boy Elon was a keen reader and learnt how to code computers.
Q. He even made his own video game called Blastar.
R. Later he moved to Canada and then the United States setting up his first company with his brother Kimbal in 1995.
S. But after some time, he sold that company to create a company called X.com.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. PQRS.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Para-jumble questions must be arranged in a logical and chronological sequence, tracing the narrative from its starting point to its conclusion.

• P must open the paragraph, as it introduces the subject in his childhood: "As a boy Elon was a keen reader and learnt how to code computers."

• Q logically follows, describing an early achievement resulting from that skill: "He even made his own video game called Blastar."

• R follows next, moving the narrative forward in time to his move to Canada/US and setting up his first company: "Later he moved to Canada and then the United States setting up his first company with his brother Kimbal in 1995."

• S concludes the paragraph, describing what happened after that company, using the connector "But after some time", which clearly refers back to the company mentioned in R: "But after some time, he sold that company to create a company called X.com."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. PQRS.

Additional Information

• Option 1: RPSQ is incorrect because it begins with R (moving to Canada/US), before the childhood context established by P has even been introduced.

• Option 2: PRSQ is incorrect because it places R (setting up the first company) before Q (making the video game as a boy), disturbing the chronological order.

• Option 3: SQRP is incorrect because it begins with S, which contains the connector "But after some time" and the phrase "that company" — both require an antecedent that has not yet been introduced.

NOTE

• Always scan for connectors ("But", "Later", "Even") and pronouns/demonstratives ("that company", "he") in jumbled sentences — they reveal which sentence must follow which.

• A sentence beginning with "But", "So", "Later", or containing "that/this + noun" almost never opens a paragraph, since it presupposes information given earlier.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
Mr. Raghav racked his brain, but couldn't think where he had left the book.
option_2: had a series of consecutive thoughts
option_3: knew it, but couldn't quite remember it
option_4: thought he had heard something before
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. thought very hard.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "to rack one's brain(s)" means to think very hard or make a great mental effort to remember or solve something. (कड़ी मशक्कत से सोचना/याद करने की कोशिश करना)
◦ Example: I racked my brain trying to recall her name, but it just wouldn't come to me.

• In the given sentence, Mr. Raghav is making a great mental effort to recall where he left the book, which is best paraphrased as "thought very hard".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2: "had a series of consecutive thoughts" is incorrect because it describes a neutral flow of thoughts, not the strained mental effort implied by "racked his brain".

• Option 3: "knew it, but couldn't quite remember it" is incorrect because it assumes he already knew the answer, whereas the idiom simply refers to the effort of thinking hard, not a state of partial knowledge.

• Option 4: "thought he had heard something before" is incorrect because it describes a vague sense of familiarity (like déjà vu), not the deliberate, strenuous act of trying to remember.

NOTE

• Related idioms of mental effort: "to put on one's thinking cap" (to think carefully about a problem), "to rack and ruin" (to fall into a state of decay — a different idiom despite the shared word "rack").

• Do not confuse "rack one's brain" with the similarly spelt "wrack" — the correct idiomatic spelling uses "rack", from the torture device that stretches/strains, reflecting mental strain.

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the underlined word.
The recent disaster of unprecedented floods in June 2013 in the state of Uttarakhand devastated many towns and villages on the banks of the rivers Bhagirathi, Pindar, Mandakini, Alaknanda and Sarju.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Familiar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Unprecedented" means never having happened or existed before; without precedent. (अभूतपूर्व)
◦ Example: The pandemic caused unprecedented disruption to global travel.

• "Familiar" means well known or common; something that has been encountered before (परिचित/जाना-पहचाना), which is the direct opposite of something that is unprecedented (never seen before).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "Lacklustre" (फीका/नीरस): Lacking energy, vitality, or brightness; unrelated to the idea of something being common or having happened before.

• Option 2: "Tarnished" (धूमिल/कलंकित): Having lost shine or reputation; relates to loss of quality or honour, not to familiarity or precedence.

• Option 4: "Deranged" (विक्षिप्त): Mentally unstable or disordered; completely unrelated in meaning to "unprecedented".

NOTE

• Other synonyms of "unprecedented": unparalleled, unheard-of, novel, groundbreaking.

• Other antonyms of "unprecedented": usual, common, routine, ordinary, customary.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Tattooing is a talent that requires a lot of time and (1)_________. There are many various kinds and (2)___________ of tattooing. Tattooing was and still is a means to communicate someone's thoughts or life by permanently (3)___________ a design of ink and colour into their flesh. The first step in tattooing is to develop an artistic (4)_________ and the skill to sketch and create your artwork. Tattooing penmanship is far more (5)___________ than sketching on paper.

Select the most appropriate answer to fill in blank 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. ability.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The passage states that tattooing is **"a talent that requires a lot of time and ______". Since tattooing is being described as a skill/talent, the missing word must refer to a related skill or capability, which is best expressed by "ability"** — the capacity or skill to do something well.

• The sentence logically pairs two things needed for a talent: "time" (a quantity) and "ability" (a skill/capacity to perform it), giving: "Tattooing is a talent that requires a lot of time and ability."

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "integrity" means honesty or moral uprightness; it does not fit the context of a skill-based talent like tattooing.

• Option 2: "capacity" generally refers to the maximum amount something can hold or produce, or a role/position — it does not naturally pair with "a lot of time" to describe a skill.

• Option 3: "liability" means a legal responsibility or a disadvantage/burden; it does not fit the context of describing a required skill.

NOTE

• In cloze passages, always read the whole passage first to understand its overall theme (here, the artistic and skill-based nature of tattooing) before choosing a word for each blank — this helps eliminate words that are semantically off-topic like "integrity" or "liability".

• Commonly confused vocabulary: ability (skill/capacity to do something) vs capacity (maximum amount that can be contained/produced) vs capability (potential to do something, often used interchangeably with ability).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Tattooing is a talent that requires a lot of time and (1)_________. There are many various kinds and (2)___________ of tattooing. Tattooing was and still is a means to communicate someone's thoughts or life by permanently (3)___________ a design of ink and colour into their flesh. The first step in tattooing is to develop an artistic (4)_________ and the skill to sketch and create your artwork. Tattooing penmanship is far more (5)___________ than sketching on paper.

Select the most appropriate answer to fill in blank 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. genres.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: **"There are many various kinds and ______ of tattooing." The word "genres" means categories or types of artistic work characterised by a particular style or form**, which pairs naturally with "kinds" to describe the different styles/categories of tattooing.

• The phrase "kinds and genres" forms a natural collocation used to describe varieties or categories within an art form, exactly as tattooing is being discussed here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "views" means opinions or perspectives (or scenic sights); it does not fit the sense of "kinds/categories" of tattooing.

• Option 3: "keys" refers to devices for locks, buttons on a device, or a musical scale; entirely unrelated to categorising types of tattoos.

• Option 4: "gestures" means movements of the body or hands to express an idea; unrelated to classifying styles of tattooing.

NOTE

• "Genre" is commonly used to classify types of art, music, literature, and film (e.g. "the horror genre", "a jazz genre") — the same idea extends naturally to tattoo styles (e.g. tribal, minimalist, realism).

• In cloze passages, look for words that pair naturally with a nearby word already in the sentence (here, "kinds and ___") to quickly narrow down the correct option.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Tattooing is a talent that requires a lot of time and (1)_________. There are many various kinds and (2)___________ of tattooing. Tattooing was and still is a means to communicate someone's thoughts or life by permanently (3)___________ a design of ink and colour into their flesh. The first step in tattooing is to develop an artistic (4)_________ and the skill to sketch and create your artwork. Tattooing penmanship is far more (5)___________ than sketching on paper.

Select the most appropriate answer to fill in blank 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. embedding.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: **"...by permanently ______ a design of ink and colour into their flesh." "Embedding" means fixing something firmly and deeply into a surrounding mass**, which precisely describes how ink is inserted into the skin during tattooing.

• The phrase "embedding...into their flesh" correctly conveys the permanent insertion of ink under the skin, which is the literal process of tattooing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "detaching" means separating or removing something — the opposite of what happens when ink is permanently placed into the skin.

• Option 3: "combining" means joining two or more things together; it does not capture the specific sense of inserting ink into flesh.

• Option 4: "fertilising" means causing an egg or plant to develop by introducing pollen or sperm, or enriching soil with nutrients — entirely unrelated to the tattooing process.

NOTE

• The preposition "into" immediately after the blank is a strong clue — it demands a verb of insertion/placement, such as "embedding", ruling out words like "detaching" (implying removal) or "combining" (implying mixing without directionality).

• Related vocabulary: "embed" (to fix firmly in a surrounding mass), "implant" (to insert/fix into tissue, especially medically), "engrave" (to cut a design into a hard surface).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Tattooing is a talent that requires a lot of time and (1)_________. There are many various kinds and (2)___________ of tattooing. Tattooing was and still is a means to communicate someone's thoughts or life by permanently (3)___________ a design of ink and colour into their flesh. The first step in tattooing is to develop an artistic (4)_________ and the skill to sketch and create your artwork. Tattooing penmanship is far more (5)___________ than sketching on paper.

Select the most appropriate answer to fill in blank 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. attitude.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: **"The first step in tattooing is to develop an artistic ______ and the skill to sketch and create your artwork." "Attitude" here refers to a settled way of thinking or an artistic outlook/mindset**, which, together with "the skill to sketch", forms the two things a beginner must develop — a creative mindset and a technical ability.

• The phrase "artistic attitude" fits the context of building an artist's mindset before developing technical drawing skills, which the sentence explicitly links with "and".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "glimpse" means a brief or partial view of something; it does not fit as something one "develops" alongside a skill.

• Option 2: "drama" refers to a play or an exciting/emotional situation; unrelated to developing an artistic mindset.

• Option 4: "career" means a chosen profession or occupation; while tattooing can be a career, the sentence is specifically about the mindset/outlook needed as "the first step", not about choosing a profession.

NOTE

• The phrase "artistic + [blank]" should modify a quality of mind or outlook (attitude, temperament, sensibility) rather than a concrete noun like "career" or "drama" — recognising the collocation pattern helps eliminate wrong options quickly.

• Related vocabulary: "aptitude" (a natural talent for something) is often confused with "attitude" (a way of thinking/feeling) in SSC vocabulary questions — the two are not interchangeable.

Tattooing is a talent that requires a lot of time and (1)_________. There are many various kinds and (2)___________ of tattooing. Tattooing was and still is a means to communicate someone's thoughts or life by permanently (3)___________ a design of ink and colour into their flesh. The first step in tattooing is to develop an artistic (4)_________ and the skill to sketch and create your artwork. Tattooing penmanship is far more (5)___________ than sketching on paper.

Select the most appropriate answer to fill in blank 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. complicated.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence reads: **"Tattooing penmanship is far more ______ than sketching on paper." "Complicated" means difficult to understand, deal with, or carry out; complex**, which fits the comparison being made — that drawing on skin (tattooing) is more difficult/complex than drawing on paper.

• The comparative structure **"far more ______ than sketching on paper" requires a word describing a degree of difficulty or complexity, which "complicated"** provides.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1: "aggravated" means made worse or more serious (often used for a situation, injury, or conflict); it does not describe the difficulty of an artistic technique.

• Option 2: "confiscated" means officially taken away/seized; entirely unrelated to describing the difficulty of tattooing versus sketching.

• Option 4: "authenticated" means verified or proven to be genuine; unrelated to the comparison of difficulty between tattooing and sketching.

NOTE

• When a blank follows a comparative structure like **"far more ___ than"**, look for an adjective that logically completes a comparison — usually describing degree, difficulty, or intensity.

• Related vocabulary: "complex" and "complicated" are near-synonyms (both mean difficult/intricate), while "complicated" often carries a slightly more negative connotation of being unnecessarily difficult.
